{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-or-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"fcf8fc0b7b4bfb7dfadde9796fd057436871c2c975c08ec1f425e65bef61ec98","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-or-class-c:lineage:15","source_registry_sha256":"ce8335c1d96ff7ed209bf236ba9a56fe92dfebd915bc0e2fa7fb830ee03f0f09","source_liveness_sha256":"c4da479589e7933e4eef7366086dfcc48a420303d0089cb0ea19ad9137abec1d"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Lane travel: curves, lane changes, passing, freeways and towing","heading":"C2 — Passing and freeway confusables: left versus right passes, no-passing exceptions, entering versus leaving a freeway, and trailer passenger rules","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Passing and freeway confusables: left versus right passes, no-passing exceptions, entering versus leaving a freeway, and trailer passenger rules
Confusable pairs from the second lane travel part, each tied to one manual page; knowledge-graph hints (group, difficulty, confusable pair) sit only in the trailing Why it matters line of each block.

FACT_ID: sec04-R01 | anchor: A01
Entering a curve you slow down first, while leaving a curve you build speed back up gradually, never the reverse. [A01]
Why it matters: group curves; confusable curve entry versus curve exit; difficulty easy.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-R02 | anchor: A01
Mirrors alone do not clear a lane change, because the blind spot cannot be seen from the seat even with mirrors, so the shoulder glance goes toward the side you are moving to. [A01]
Why it matters: group lane changes; confusable mirror check versus shoulder glance; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-R03 | anchor: A02
Cutting back in too soon after a pass risks sideswiping the vehicle you passed, while staying out too long risks a head-on crash with oncoming traffic. [A02]
Why it matters: group passing; confusable early return versus late return; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-R04 | anchor: A02
A pass must begin no earlier than the start of the passing zone and be finished before the no-passing zone, so both ends of the pass are fixed by the zone. [A02]
Why it matters: group passing; confusable starting point versus finishing point; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-R05 | anchor: A02
After a pass you signal and move back into your lane once the vehicle you passed is visible in your rearview mirror. [A02]
Why it matters: group passing; confusable return cue versus starting cue; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-R06 | anchor: A03
In a no-passing zone, crossing the center line is still allowed to turn left or when the right side of the road is blocked, but never to pass. [A03]
Why it matters: group no-passing; confusable passing versus left turn or blocked lane; difficulty hard.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-R07 | anchor: A03
Passing is banned when the vehicle ahead has stopped at a crosswalk for a pedestrian, just as it is banned near intersections and railroad crossings. [A03]
Why it matters: group no-passing; confusable crosswalk stop versus intersection ban; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-R08 | anchor: A04
Passing a left-turning vehicle on the right is allowed only on pavement and outside the bike lane, whereas passing on the right on a multi-lane road needs the slower vehicle to be in the left lane. [A04]
Why it matters: group passing on the right; confusable turning-vehicle case versus multi-lane case; difficulty hard.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-R09 | anchor: A04
When you are being passed, you help by keeping right and adjusting speed, but you must not wave the driver on or flash your signals to tell them when to go. [A04]
Why it matters: group being passed; confusable helping a pass versus signaling a pass; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-R10 | anchor: A05
Entering a freeway is the reverse of entering most busy roads: instead of slowing or stopping, you speed up on the ramp and merge. [A05]
Why it matters: group freeway entry; confusable busy-road entry versus freeway entry; difficulty easy.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R11 | anchor: A05
Several light taps on the brake pedal are how you warn drivers behind you that freeway traffic ahead is slowing. [A05]
Why it matters: group freeway driving; confusable warning taps versus steady braking; difficulty easy.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R12 | anchor: A05
Keeping pace with freeway traffic is encouraged, but the posted speed still caps you, and a driver below the flow belongs in the right lane. [A05]
Why it matters: group freeway driving; confusable keeping pace versus exceeding the limit; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R13 | anchor: A06
A ramp meter that shows green lets one vehicle go, while a dark ramp meter is off and requires no stop at all. [A06]
Why it matters: group ramp meters; confusable green meter versus dark meter; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R14 | anchor: A06
Leaving a freeway, you hold your speed until you are off the freeway and slow down only on the exit ramp, not in the travel lanes. [A06]
Why it matters: group freeway exit; confusable slowing on the ramp versus slowing on the freeway; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R15 | anchor: A06
A missed exit means driving on to the next one, while stopping or backing up on the freeway is never allowed and the shoulder is for emergencies only. [A06]
Why it matters: group freeway exit; confusable next exit versus backing up; difficulty easy.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R16 | anchor: A07
A fifth-wheel trailer may carry passengers only when it has safety glazing, a way to signal the driver and an exit that opens from both sides, while trailers outside the listed exceptions may not carry passengers at all. [A07]
Why it matters: group towing; confusable fifth-wheel trailer versus ordinary trailer; difficulty hard.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec04-R17 | anchor: A07
One boat, utility trailer or other vehicle may be towed behind a passenger or recreational vehicle, but adding a second towed unit is not allowed. [A07]
Why it matters: group towing; confusable single tow versus double tow; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0044]
